clue.text: One who takes each issue as it comes

definitions.text: One who takes each issue as it comes

clue.text: Disturbed at noise in the country

clue.text: University element will go around as one

parts.note: tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A university department will circulate as a single body.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one in counting.

clue.text: Sailors love to be free — so acquit

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, so sailors

indicators.note: the letters are set free from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors want to love freely, so pardon them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like a release from a charge, matching 'acquit', but 'to be free' is the anagram signal for the four-letter word for love.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to clear them of guilt, a synonym of acquit.

clue.text: Conductor's support for uplifting alternative string sound

explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is the raised platform on which an orchestral conductor stands.

clue.text: Article on name-dropping?

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, used where an author's name has been omitted.

clue.text: Eastern manoeuvres deserving to be taken seriously

indicators.note: manoeuvres move the word's letters into new positions

clue.text: Act badly, avoiding punishment, and leave in style

parts.note: to get away is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves, escapes punishment and departs elegantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do wrong and escape any penalty for it.

clue.text: Merit attention, as very good workers do — and very bad ones!

clue.text: Necessarily involves a silent working

explanation.surface: Something requires a silent operation.

clue.text: Christian names should include hers

clue.text: Very light, for example

parts.note: reads as an intensified adjective of weight

clue.text: France's summer celebration

été is French for summer

clue.text: He is stubbornly resolved to leave part out

clue.text: Caviare might produce such greed

clue.text: Well-known Russian cocktail?

clue.text: Reckon to keep fit

explanation.definitionFit: Work out means both to calculate and to exercise.

A plus MP, a member of parliament

clue.text: Beat, after exciting recount

clue.text: Interrupts and adds one's contribution

definitions.meaning: to pay a share toward a total

clue.text: Slight wound, sustaining no handicap

definitions.meaning: a minor cut on the skin

clue.text: Spell it back to me

indicators.note: back reads the little word in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Unruly child stuck in algebra test

clue.text: Raise 51 feet

parts.note: sounds like a boxer knocked out by one punch, but a light boxer could be blown out like a plume
